title: RIDE SHARING (UBER)
subtitle: Four problems in one: a flood of location updates, matching, locking drivers, and a multi-step trip lifecycle.
footer: DDIA: Ch 8 leases · Ch 3 geo index · Ch 6 partition by region   ·   Similar: Live comments · Collaborative editor · Stock trading · Online auction

items: Driver locations are ephemeral and frequent, so keep them in Redis's geospatial index, not a database.
Offer a ride to one driver at a time and lock that driver with a short TTL so they can't get two offers.
Run ride requests through a durable, per-region queue so a crashed matcher loses nothing.
Rider requests a ride (pickup, destination) and sees a fare estimate
Match to a nearby available driver; driver accepts or declines
Live location of driver during the trip
Match within ~1 minute
A driver is never assigned two rides (consistency)
High availability for location updates
Handle surge peaks per city
1M active drivers × 1 update/4s = 250k location writes/s, ephemeral (only the latest matters).
Ride requests ~100/s avg.

blocks.text: Naive: drivers write locations to Postgres. 250k writes/sec of throwaway data breaks it.

items: Locations go to Redis GEO: in memory, latest point only, with TTL. GEOSEARCH finds drivers within radius.
Matching offers the ride to one driver at a time and takes a lock on that driver (SET NX with a 10s TTL), so they can't be offered two rides.
Requests go through a durable queue partitioned by region, so a crashed matcher doesn't lose rides and surges scale per city.
Driver double-assigned?
Lock per driver with TTL = accept window, plus conditional assignment in Postgres. Lock expiry = automatic decline.
Reduce location load?
Adaptive update frequency (less when stationary), client batching.
Why not query Postgres + PostGIS?
Fine for reads, but 250k updates/sec of ephemeral data belongs in memory.
Matcher crash mid-match?
Durable workflow/queue; the request is re-processed and idempotent by ride_id.
Offering a ride to many drivers at once without locks, so two drivers accept the same ride.
Adding parts before a number shows they are needed.
Ignoring retries, timeouts and crashes.
